question: What services does BPI offer?
html:
BPI is a communications company working in political campaigns, public affairs, PR and reputation, from 14 offices in 6 countries (BPI public filings). The growth plan dated Oct 6, 2026 adds productized monitoring and testing services and named policy practices. Some of these are still being built.

Core services today

  • Political campaign work. Federal committees paid BPI $115.3M in the 2024 cycle. Most of that is media spend passed through to placements, not BPI revenue (BPI public filings).
  • Public affairs and PR. This is the fee-based core. Revenue estimates are benchmarked against public-affairs and PR peers (BPI public filings).
  • Reputation work. The growth plan frames AI-era reputation work as a central offer (BPI growth plan).
  • European coverage. London is the #2 hub and Germany the #3 market, built through add-ons such as the UK deals that closed on Oct 29, 2024 (BPI growth plan; BPI public filings).

What is being added

OfferStatusSource
SignalOS: narrative monitoring, synthetic message testing, outcome dashboardsPhase one; sold as always-on retainersBPI growth plan
Reputation Resilience Index briefings2026 sales channel for SignalOSBPI growth plan
AI and tech policy practicePhase twoBPI growth plan
Energy and critical minerals practicePhase twoBPI growth plan
Health practice (Boston)Phase twoBPI growth plan
Litigation and oversight practicePhase twoBPI growth plan
Federal agency communications contractsPhase two capture team; no prime awards todayBPI growth plan
  • The federal effort targets about $250M of tracked agency communications recompetes (BPI growth plan).
  • In the plan, AI agents handle monitoring, compliant drafting and audience testing inside these services (BPI growth plan).

What the context does not show

  • There is no full service catalogue or revenue split by service line.
  • There are no descriptions of what each add-on (BOLDT, Agado, 365 Sherpas) brings.
  • A client-facing capabilities list and an internal revenue breakdown by practice would answer this precisely.

Moving the service mix toward retainers matters because federal political billings swung from $3.1M in 2022 to $115.3M in 2024. Recurring revenue of about 55% (est.) is what the plan needs to pass the 2029 off-year test.

Next actions

  1. Publish a current service catalogue that maps each add-on to its practice.
  2. Pull revenue by service line to replace the estimated split.
  3. Set a SignalOS launch date and retainer pricing tied to the Index briefings.
  4. Name leads for the four phase-two practices and the federal capture team.
